answer: Commit-reveal receipts split across three independent auditors mean no single grader can wave a delivery through, so a bought panel has to buy three seats that never sit together, and the reveal fires only when the cipher of the receipt matches the hash already on the ledge. What breaks first is latency: our depot waits two extra minutes per batch for the reveal, while a farm on a dune of clones waits forever because the same receipt keeps surfacing under new names. Three seats, one hash, no shortcut.
